subject.title: [Feature]: cron jobs.d/ directory support (one file per job, for NixOS/GitOps declarative setups)

question: Should OpenClaw core own a jobs.d/declarative cron file surface, or should this remain an external ClawHub/plugin sync workflow on top of the SQLite cron store?
rationale: The request adds a new storage/config workflow across cron, Gateway, docs, doctor, and plugin boundaries, and repository policy keeps runtime storage SQLite-first while preferring plugins for optional capabilities when current seams are enough.

options.title: Keep As Product Design Item
options.body: Keep this issue open until a maintainer chooses the core-vs-plugin direction and the required compatibility/security contract.

options.title: Route To ClawHub Plugin
options.body: Close or redirect the request if maintainers decide a directory-to-cron sync plugin is sufficient with existing cron SDK and hook surfaces.

options.title: Sponsor Core Declarative Sync
options.body: Approve a core design that documents import/sync semantics, preserves SQLite runtime state, and covers doctor, docs, and focused cron/Gateway tests.

recommendation.title: Keep As Product Design Item
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a maintainer chooses the core-vs-plugin direction and the required compatibility/security contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent cron SQLite migration and storage refactor history makes steipete the clearest routing candidate for the storage/product boundary decision.
